0.0.n: 皆さん politely addresses all the viewers.

0.1.n: A standard daytime greeting; its final は is pronounced わ.

0.3.n: YUKI is the speaker’s name, written in Latin letters.

0.4.n: です politely identifies the speaker; Japanese leaves out I here.

1.0.n: 私 refers to the speaker and is suitable for polite introductions.

1.1.n: は marks 私 as the topic: who this sentence is about.

1.2.n: 匹 counts small animals; 6匹 is read ろっぴき.

1.3.n: の connects the animal count to ハムスター, telling us how many there are.

1.4.n: This borrowed word is written in katakana; Japanese nouns do not change form for plurals.

1.5.n: This と joins the hamsters and cats into one list.

1.7.n: 匹 is also used to count cats; 6匹 is read ろっぴき.

1.8.n: の links the count 6匹 to 猫.

1.9.n: 猫 can mean one cat or several; 6匹 makes the number clear here.

1.10.n: This と marks the animals as the companions the speaker lives with.

1.11.n: 暮らす becomes 暮らして + います, politely describing an ongoing living situation.

2.0.n: これから points to what the speaker will do starting now.

2.1.n: 日本語 names the language; 語 means language here.

2.2.n: で marks the language used for speaking.

2.4.n: 私 combines with たち here to refer to the speaker and her animals.

2.5.n: Added to 私, たち makes 私たち, meaning we.

2.6.n: の links 私たち to 幸せな日々, making those days ours.

2.7.n: 幸せ describes 日々 and needs な before that noun.

2.8.n: な connects the describing word 幸せ to the noun 日々.

2.9.n: 日々 refers to daily life; 々 repeats the preceding character.

2.10.n: を marks 幸せな日々 as what the speaker will talk about.

2.11.n: お話しする is a respectful way to say talk; ていきます politely presents this as continuing into the future.

0.tip: Japanese often leaves out I when the speaker’s identity is clear.

1.lit: I, as for, six small animals of hamsters and six small animals of cats with am living.
1.tip: The first と means and, while the second と means with.

2.lit: From now on, in Japanese, our happy days will talk about going forward.
2.tip: A verb’s て-form plus いきます can describe an action continuing into the future, rather than physical movement.
